headline: COP31 ends in Antalya with no overall climate deal after a split over fossil fuels, as Russian missiles land in Poland and Ghana's Black Challenge become amputee football world champions.

items.title: Russian missiles and a drone come down inside Poland
items.summary: Poland says two missiles and a jet-powered drone landed in its south-east during Russia's overnight attack on Ukraine on 20 November, with no injuries. PM Tusk called it a deliberate provocation and NATO's Rutte a grave violation; President Trump said Putin did it by mistake.
items.videoQuery: Russian missiles land in Poland November 2026

items.title: Heavy Russian strikes follow Ukraine's hit on the Crimean Bridge
items.summary: After a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed in a Ukrainian strike, Russia launched hundreds of drones and over 100 missiles, and Kyiv Independent counted at least 2 dead and 83 injured on 21 November, mostly in Kryvyi Rih. Moscow calls the barrages retaliation; Kyiv says the bridge carried military supplies.
items.videoQuery: Crimean bridge strike Russia retaliation Kryvyi Rih

items.title: US floats NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine
items.summary: After a Berlin meeting of Ukraine's backers, Jared Kushner said Russia could accept Article 5-style guarantees and that Trump is open to them. Russia's deputy foreign minister called any quasi-membership unacceptable, and Zelensky said there is no shared understanding yet of what the guarantees mean.

items.title: COP31 in Antalya ends with no overall deal
items.summary: After two days of overtime, the longest UN climate summit on record closed on 22 November without adopting its main 'Antalya Pact' text, which left out any commitment to move away from fossil fuels. The EU formally objected; UN chief Guterres said he was deeply disappointed and that the science is unambiguous.
items.why: No new global push this year: carbon markets and national action (like Ghana's Article 6 deals) carry more of the load.

items.title: Ghana speaks for Africa: shortfalls, but no block on consensus
items.summary: Speaking for the African Group, Ghana said the text fell short on climate finance, loss and damage and a just transition, but that Africa would not stand in the way. Panama and the Marshall Islands rejected the outcome, while Saudi Arabia, for Arab states, defended references to carbon capture.
items.why: Ghana's voice in the African Group is a good case study for policy-focused master's applications.

items.title: What survived: carbon markets, adaptation and a road to Addis Ababa
items.summary: Separate decisions on carbon markets, the Adaptation Fund, transparency and a just-transition work programme went through, and a finance road map on adaptation will report at COP32 in Addis Ababa. The text puts developing countries' needs at US$5.1–6.8 trillion through 2030 but sets no plan to deliver it.
items.why: COP32 will be in Africa (Ethiopia) in 2027, a big stage for African carbon projects.
items.videoQuery: COP32 Addis Ababa climate finance road map

items.title: US absent again; Panama says it won't be held hostage by oil producers
items.summary: The United States sent no delegation for a second year. A France- and Panama-led coalition from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific rejected a draft that dropped earlier fossil-fuel phase-out language; current national plans point to just over 2.5°C of warming.
items.videoQuery: COP31 fossil fuel debate no agreement

items.title: Mahama asks Minority to back the $10bn New Economy programme
items.summary: President Mahama urged the opposition Minority to support the $10bn New Economy programme even if its success helps keep the NDC in power. Officials separately said two pharmaceutical hubs are planned under the plan.
items.why: Big public programmes create openings for suppliers, partners and green-industry pitches.

items.title: Kisseman–Christian Village bridge in Accra to close for six months
items.summary: The bridge will shut to traffic for reconstruction and raising under the Greater Accra Resilient and Integrated Development (GARID) project, aimed at reducing flooding.
items.why: Plan Accra trips around the closure.

items.title: Dozens missing after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal
items.summary: A boat carrying an estimated 50–100 people overturned near Yenne, south of Dakar; four bodies were recovered. The IOM estimates at least 454 people have died or gone missing off the West African coast this year.

items.title: Two in five African children live near armed conflict
items.summary: Save the Children says about 260 million African children lived within 50 km of fighting in 2025, roughly 20% more than in 2024 and 44% of the world total.

items.title: Wall Street's longest losing streak since 2024
items.summary: US stocks kept falling into Friday, with the Dow down about 1,100 points in one session, as worries about AI stocks and the chance of further US interest-rate rises hit markets. Asian shares came under pressure as the new week opened.
items.why: Higher US rates usually mean tighter money for emerging markets like Ghana and pricier climate finance.
items.videoQuery: Wall Street losing streak Dow drops 1100 points

items.title: US-led group wins Kenya's Mrima Hill critical-minerals tender
items.summary: Kenya picked Frontier Minerals, a US-led consortium, for the Mrima Hill niobium and rare-earths deposit, valued at about Ksh8 trillion (over $60bn), ahead of Chinese bidders. A rival has challenged the award, and the firm says it wants to refine locally.
items.why: Shows the US–China race for African critical minerals and the push for local processing, as in Ghana's 2030 plans.

items.title: Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth
items.summary: On 18 November NASA's Voyager 1 passed about 25.9 billion km from Earth, so its signal takes a full day to arrive. NASA has had no data from it since 14 November and engineers are investigating.

items.title: Alzheimer's risk gene works through the brain's cleanup cells
items.summary: University of Virginia researchers found the CASS4 gene acts mainly in microglia, the immune cells that contain amyloid plaques; disrupting it in mice sped up plaque build-up and memory decline. Human effects are still untested.

items.title: Keto diet cut liver fat most in a small trial
items.summary: In a 42-person trial, keto, Mediterranean and low-fat plant diets all led to about 10% weight loss, but liver fat fell 67% on keto versus 45% on the others. The study was small and short.

items.title: Einstein's relativity bends a textbook chemistry rule
items.summary: Brown University chemists found that in a carbon–bismuth molecule, relativistic effects blur the usual split between sigma and pi bonds. The work, in Science, may matter for bismuth-based solar and quantum materials.

good.title: Ghana's Black Challenge are amputee football world champions
good.summary: Ghana beat Morocco 1–0 in Mexico to win their first World Amputee Football World Cup, after knocking out holders Türkiye on penalties. Forward Mubarik Mohammed won the Golden Boot with seven goals.
good.videoQuery: Black Challenge Ghana Amputee World Cup final Morocco

good.title: West Africa's first paediatric neuro-oncologist is Ghanaian
good.summary: Dr Ernestina Schandorf of Korle Bu finished a St Jude fellowship; yearly admissions of children with brain tumours to her unit have risen from three to 17 and she set up a regular tumour board.
good.why: An overseas fellowship that built capacity at home: a model for study abroad plans.

good.title: Dak'Art Biennale opens with 54 African artists
good.summary: Senegal's contemporary art biennale brings together 54 artists from 17 African countries around resilience and rebound, running until 19 December.

good.title: AI spots bladder cancer signs up to five years early
good.summary: A University of Plymouth model trained on about 70,000 Welsh health records caught 85% of bladder cancer cases and outperformed NHS referral rules, though it still needs testing elsewhere.

good.title: New weight-loss drug halves knee pain for many patients
good.summary: In phase 3 trials of over 1,000 people with knee osteoarthritis and obesity, about two-thirds on the top dose of retatrutide had their knee pain at least halved, versus 38% on placebo. The drug is not yet approved.

quiz.q: Which country spoke for the African Group in COP31's closing session?
quiz.why: Ghana said the text fell short on finance and just transition but Africa would not block consensus.
The adaptation finance road map is due to report at COP32 in Addis Ababa.

quiz.q: Whom did Ghana's Black Challenge beat in the Amputee World Cup final?
quiz.why: Ghana won 1–0 for their first world title.

future.title: Clean cooking financed by carbon credits
future.why: New government policies across Africa have helped secure about $900 million in new clean-cooking finance, with carbon credits as the main engine. The catch: it only lasts if buyers trust the credits.
future.fit: This is Carbon Clarity's core. The winners will be projects with measured, audit-ready data.
future.step: This month: map which Gold Standard metered-method requirements your pilot data already meets.

future.title: Digital MRV and high-integrity credit data
future.why: Credit buyers increasingly pay only for credits they can verify. Sensor-based monitoring and clean data trails are becoming the difference between credits that sell and credits that don't.
future.fit: Your Data Vault idea could become a service for other cookstove and agriculture projects in Ghana.
future.step: Write a one-page description of the Data Vault as a service: who pays, what it proves.

future.title: Clean heat for small industries
future.why: RMI lists clean industrial heat among Africa's six emerging climate-tech opportunities. Fish smoking is exactly this: small-scale process heat.
future.fit: Improved ovens for fish processors are a clean-heat business with income for women, not just a stove programme.
future.step: Estimate the market: how many processors in Greater Accra and coastal Ghana, and how much wood they burn.

future.title: Carbon removal from biomass: biochar
future.why: RMI also highlights carbon dioxide removal that uses Africa's biomass and soils, a market where removal credits sell for far more than avoidance credits.
future.fit: Waste biomass from smoking (husks, offcuts) could be turned into biochar: a second revenue stream.
future.step: Read one biochar removal methodology and list what you'd need to measure.

future.title: Energy-led climate tech is where African investment goes
future.why: Africa's climate-tech startups raised $6.35bn from 2016 to 2025, now the continent's biggest venture sector, with energy taking about 65% of the money.
future.fit: Pitch Carbon Clarity as energy plus livelihoods: efficient heat, solar drying or cold storage for fish.
future.step: Add one slide to your pitch: 'Why energy investors should care about fish smoking'.

future.title: Article 6 advisory for Ghanaian projects
future.why: Ghana is one of the first countries trading credits between governments under Article 6. Developers need people who understand authorisation, corresponding adjustments and the Carbon Market Office process.
future.fit: Your Ghana carbon market research makes you one of those people: it can become consulting work or a job.
future.step: Turn your Step 3 agreement table into a two-page brief you can share on LinkedIn.
